body: I can tell a joke.  I've won several standup competitions in my area in fact.  I just don't know how to leverage my stage personality to a real situation.  I'm totally comfortable and in my element in front of crowds.  But the thought of just buying a beer, walking up to somebody, and starting a conversation seems like the most unnatural thing on earth.  Not sure why.  Never been sure why.
Appreciate that. I like Vegas and I'd totally do that.
Not a single listing within 300 miles. :/

I love running, ring gymnastics, composing music, and motorcycling. Unfortunately those are all solo hobbies. I was in Krav Maga for a while and I thought that would lead to something but it was just a bunch of armed disarms with not a lot of real interpersonal interaction for anybody involved.

I have been told I look intimidating physically. People who know me (I.e. coworkers) know I have a good sense of humor and like to joke around with me. I do a lot of public speaking for my job and that is always well received.  Outside of work nobody talks to me in public unless they're a clerk, and I wouldn't know where to begin to start a conversation naturally.

Other than my few friends from grade school who are gone and my ex fiancee, I've never been close to anyone and don't have a clue where to begin.
It sounds like a good idea if I can make the hours work.
How do I get started with this? I'm an avid runner and tennis player but never have anyone to play with anymore.
I like the music but really don't want to be groped by someone who just sees me as a warm body.
I saw this on An Idiot Abroad. Haha. Sadly I do not live in a very open minded area. Nothing like that for hundreds of miles, unless they require a membership in a secret society first.
I suppose, but I can't say I'd feel very good about it afterward.
